incidents.vector: Not specified in available reporting.
incidents.impact: A threat actor stole personal data belonging to more than 11.7 million Capcom gamers, mostly usernames, emails and account technical details.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime and sea-shipping companies (CyberLogitec customers)
incidents.vector: The group, n0n, compromised CyberLogitec, a South Korean maritime IT platform provider whose website has been down for weeks, and pivoted from that foothold into downstream customer networks.
incidents.impact: More than 40 port authorities, ship managers and shipping logistics firms across 18 countries were listed on n0n's leak site demanding a combined $1.2 billion in ransom; most victims refused to pay and had their data published. It is one of the largest cyberattacks on the maritime sector since NotPetya in 2016.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Quest's Quanum Lab Services Manager (LSM) portal, used by clinicians to place test orders and retrieve results.
incidents.impact: Quest took the Quanum LSM system offline and believes some patient data was accessed; no hacking group has claimed responsibility, and the company said lab testing operations and the recent PHP vulnerabilities were not involved.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached cloud platform Railway.com and stole encrypted environment variables from customer accounts, likely decrypting some to obtain API keys and credentials.
incidents.impact: Railway believes the incident is part of a larger wave of attacks against AI providers and notified affected AI providers so they could revoke exposed customer API keys.

incidents.vector: Not specified in available reporting.
incidents.impact: Hackers breached the South Korean coffee and tea chain and stole data on 2.76 million customers.

incidents.vector: Not specified in available reporting.
incidents.impact: A cyberattack against German group TAKKT's food services division disrupted food delivery services across North America.

incidents.victim: ccTLD registries for American Samoa (.as), Ghana (.gh) and Sierra Leone (.sl)
incidents.vector: Attackers modified DNS records for the hijacked ccTLDs to pass domain-ownership checks and fraudulently obtain HTTPS certificates for specific domains.
incidents.impact: Google said the threat actor targeted some of its services as well as other organizations using the hijacked domain infrastructure.

incidents.victim: ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers (2,250+ Microsoft 365 tenants)
incidents.vector: Storm-0940 compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup application credentials, then used the open-source agentic AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX to automate password-spraying (up to 2,900 attempts/minute) and OAuth application abuse against downstream tenants.
incidents.impact: The actor attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants and achieved privileged cloud persistence — including credential and privilege changes — at multiple organizations within three hours of targeting; ConnectWise suspended its Cloud Backup, SaaS Security and Cloud Management services and began restoring them in phases starting Oct. 22.

incidents.vector: A flawed April 2025 HSM key-generation ceremony produced eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys with only a handful of bits of entropy — one key was simply the number 4 — letting anyone derive the private keys directly from the public certificates.
incidents.impact: Chrome, Firefox, Apple and Microsoft blocked the affected certificates; eMudhra revoked them and announced it is exiting the SSL/TLS certificate business entirely, with shares falling 40%. The Go team also shipped patched releases (CVE-2026-111943) that reject the compromised keys across Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform and other cloud-native tooling.

incidents.vector: Two unauthenticated memory-corruption flaws in PHP's core Zend engine (out-of-memory handling and stale request state), triggerable via crafted multipart file-upload requests, allow remote code execution before any application code runs.
incidents.impact: Palo Alto Networks and Censys estimated 22.6-41 million potentially exposed instances; exploitation attempts (scanning, botnet recruitment) have been widespread since disclosure, but as of Oct. 23 researchers had not confirmed any successful mass compromise, and SANS returned its Infocon to green after the feared wave of exploitation failed to materialize. Hundreds of websites and government services went offline as precautionary shutdowns.

incidents.vector: The city's IT department identified suspicious activity on municipal systems; no group has claimed responsibility and the initial access method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The attack knocked out the MyColaSC utility-payment platform, GIS systems, and animal services, though police, fire, 911 and water systems remained operational.

incidents.vector: Not specified in available reporting.
incidents.impact: Hackers breached India's largest bank and stole data on almost 4,000 customers, prompting renewed scrutiny of cyber defenses at Indian banks.

incidents.vector: Attackers used a developer's GitHub account — compromised seven months earlier via a malicious Open VSX extension installed on a personal device — to push a secrets-stealing binary into OVHcloud's open-source command-line tool, enabled by a release-immutability misconfiguration.
incidents.impact: The poisoned CLI binary was live for about 90 minutes and downloaded roughly 250 times before OVHcloud detected and removed it.

incidents.vector: An infostealer was added to LiteLLM version 1.107.0 and published to its official Docker and PyPI releases, searching for and exfiltrating cloud credentials, developer secrets and AI provider API keys.
incidents.impact: Organizations that pulled the compromised release risked exposure of cloud and AI-provider credentials; this is LiteLLM's second supply-chain security incident this year after it was also hit in the earlier Trivy compromise.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure organizations across the Americas, Europe and Australia (~600 victims)
incidents.vector: SafePay actors gain initial access via compromised credentials and known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN devices, then use legitimate IT tools to move laterally, delete or disable backups, exfiltrate data and encrypt systems.
incidents.impact: CISA, FBI, USSS and international partners say SafePay has impacted roughly 600 victims in 2026, making it one of the most active ransomware groups this year; actors threaten to leak stolen data and call victims directly to pressure payment.

incidents.victim: John Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins and 100+ other websites
incidents.vector: A suspected Chinese hacker used the DeepSeek and Claude Code AI tools to automate the compromise of more than 100 websites, reportedly spending only about $5,000 worth of tokens.
incidents.impact: Victims included well-known manufacturers; researchers say the low-cost, AI-driven campaign illustrates how agentic AI is lowering the barrier to mass website compromise.

incidents.vector: A Chinese organized crime group gained access to Staples' internal "Nexus" application and used it to issue fraudulent gift cards.
incidents.impact: The group issued more than 15,000 gift cards worth over $5 million for retailers including Target and Sephora, using them to buy electronics and other goods shipped to China for resale.

incidents.vector: Hackers used stolen credentials to access a Nikkei cloud server.
incidents.impact: The Japanese media conglomerate's third security breach in a month resulted in the theft of 1.83 million records.

incidents.victim: Multiple Indian universities and an e-commerce site
incidents.vector: An actor dubbed BUGSTER used a jailbroken AI agent framework (Hermes Agent with DeepSeek V4) to automate reconnaissance, WordPress brute-forcing, and database exfiltration against target networks, primarily in India.
incidents.impact: The actor exfiltrated a database of more than 5,200 student and faculty records containing personal information from one university and compromised a second university's WordPress site; the same operator also built AI-assisted VoIP fraud, Wi-Fi password-cracking, and cryptocurrency reconnaissance tooling.

incidents.vector: A hacker breached the Japanese VPS provider and installed malware across its Desktop Cloud server fleet, seeking credentials for trading and securities tools.
incidents.impact: More than 26,700 servers were infected before Onamae shut down all affected servers within a day of detecting the breach.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the Japanese securities firm's Tradeworks internet trading system.
incidents.impact: Attackers accessed data on nearly 5,000 traders and placed unauthorized purchase orders on at least seven accounts, apparently to test their access; the orders were described by the firm as "unintentional."

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited wallet seed phrases generated with insufficient randomness on affected iOS and macOS clients.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole $1.4 million from user accounts; Qubic halted operations and froze about 87% of the stolen funds while working to restore them to customers.

incidents.vector: Not specified in available reporting.
incidents.impact: The attack crippled Radiocom's internal IT network, forcing the state-owned broadcaster to shut down its email server; the radio and TV broadcast network itself was not affected.

incidents.vector: A Russian-speaking threat actor gained access to an exposed Elasticsearch server belonging to the platform.
incidents.impact: Approximately 6.8 million documents were stolen from the platform.

incidents.vector: A hacker breached AfD's web hosting provider.
incidents.impact: 281GB of internal data was leaked, including email inboxes, website databases, and internal private documents.

incidents.victim: Ledger Nano X customers who purchased devices via reseller CryptoBilis
incidents.vector: A Southeast Asian reseller, CryptoBilis, distributed Ledger Nano X hardware wallets implanted with spy chips.
incidents.impact: Ledger told affected customers to discard the compromised devices and move funds to new blockchain addresses to prevent theft.

incidents.vector: Attackers used stolen service account credentials to access internal PingCAP systems between Sept. 9 and Oct. 7, 2026, copying data and source code.
incidents.impact: Exfiltrated data included billing/business records, encrypted API keys, Jira tickets and customer connection logs; FulcrumSec claims broader access, including a replicated internal database, and has named downstream enterprises such as Airbnb, Booking.com, Baidu, Capcom, Konami and Square Enix as exposed. PingCAP says no customer TiDB databases were accessed.

incidents.victim: 20+ Japanese companies (GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae reported up to 80)
incidents.vector: A Chinese open-source AI penetration-testing agent, ARTEX, was used to automate attacks against Japanese corporate networks — the same framework linked to the Storm-0940/ConnectWise campaign and attacks on South Korean banks.
incidents.impact: Japanese security firm GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae concluded ARTEX was used in attacks against roughly 80 Japanese companies, with eight occurring in the 30 days before its report.

incidents.victim: TeamUpdraft and its WordPress plugin customers
incidents.vector: Hackers accessed TeamUpdraft's backend database and stole customer accounts and site connection keys.
incidents.impact: Attackers used the stolen connection keys to connect directly to customer sites and deploy malicious plugins, according to security firm Wordfence.

incidents.vector: Not specified in available reporting.
incidents.impact: The German smart home and building automation company shut down its internal IT network to contain an intrusion; the incident did not spread to customer systems, which run on localized mini-servers.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited an Oracle PeopleSoft platform at Accenture that the company had failed to patch despite available security updates.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters stole personal and business data on nearly all FBI special agents; the FBI subsequently dropped Accenture as a contractor over the failure to secure the breached systems.

incidents.vector: Not specified in available reporting.
incidents.impact: The Canadian supermarket chain disclosed a data breach and notified customers that their personal data was stolen in the incident.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a website operated by department store brand Hankyu Hanshin.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole the data of 1.26 million customers in the breach.

incidents.victim: Zeabur (AI DevOps platform) and its customers
incidents.vector: A hacker stole environment variables and other account records in the platform's second breach of the year, following an earlier AWS backend compromise in August.
incidents.impact: More than 320,000 accounts were affected; Zeabur announced it will shut down entirely at the end of 2026 as a result.

incidents.vector: An unidentified third party misused the Japanese software company's member-information retrieval API to pull customer records in bulk.
incidents.impact: The breach compromised 22,519,960 customer records containing names, emails, passwords, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and employment information.

incidents.victim: French and other European grocery/retail chains (Intermarché/Netto and 700+ stores)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited unpatched vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-41450, -41451, -41452) in Danfoss AK-SM 800A and related Dixell/Copeland XWEB refrigeration controllers, reversing defrost cycles to heat units while disguising the activity as routine maintenance.
incidents.impact: More than 700 grocery and retail stores across France, Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium had refrigeration systems sabotaged overnight, spoiling food and causing small fires; Intermarché alone reported tens of millions of euros in losses.

incidents.victim: IDCFrontier (Japanese cloud provider) and downstream customers
incidents.vector: Not specified in available reporting.
incidents.impact: A ransomware attack on the Japanese cloud provider disrupted services for 495 companies and local governments that rely on its hosting.

incidents.vector: An unidentified actor hacked more than 330 Tor relays, infected them with Ebury Linux malware, and converted them into malicious exit relays to intercept SSH connections and downgrade/intercept unencrypted email traffic.
incidents.impact: More than 10% of Tor exit relays were compromised over a three-day window before detection and blocklisting — one of the largest security incidents in Tor's history.
